picks.excerpt: Amazon expanded Kindle Translate (beta) to five new language pairs: English paired with Spanish, German, French, Italian and Portuguese. Self-published KDP authors can auto-translate and publish 'with a few clicks'; every translation passes an automated quality review before going live, authors can preview and set pricing, and translated titles can enroll in Kindle Unlimited. Amazon notes historically fewer than 5% of Amazon.com titles exist in more than one language. Kindle Translate launched Nov 2025 (EN<->ES, DE->EN); this is its first big language expansion.

Emaqi, the digital manga platform from Tokyo-based Orange Inc., launched a $6.99/month premium subscription for North American English-language readers with 26,000+ volumes across ~2,500 series from major Japanese publishers (incl. Attack on Titan, upcoming Viz releases). Emaqi uses AI-assisted programs to translate, letter and produce its manga exclusives, compressing the localization pipeline. 7-day free trial plus reader incentive programs.

Guest post arguing that AI already has a legitimate role in scholarly peer review and that journal/publisher policies — many of which flatly ban AI in review — need updating with practical guidance instead of prohibition. Site byline date June 30, 2026.

ROUNDUP, but carries one otherwise-uncovered story: Dutch publishers VBK, WPG, Lannoo and Maven plus distributor CB launched Bookpact.ai, a platform letting publishers (with author consent) control and monetize AI use of their books on an opt-in, title-by-title basis — training, summarization, translation and quotation each licensed as separate use cases with separate terms, plus traceable usage reporting. No single-story coverage exists on any allowed domain (only IPA/publishersmarketplace outside the pool). Roundup's other AI items (Kobo 45% rejections, ElevenLabs Michael Caine Odyssey) are ALREADY PUBLISHED as cards — the card angle must be Bookpact only.
